facts.question: Native 'amount off products' 10% on won-e2e-simple-a only, minimumRequirement subtotal that the WHOLE cart (A+B) exceeds but A alone does not. Cart = A+B: does the discount apply?

setup.cartCurrency: CZK (storefront session resolved to the cesko market; converted line prices: A=218.00, B=262.00, cart total=480.00)
setup.note: The 15.00 USD minimum converts to roughly 327 CZK at the live exchange rate used by Shopify for this session: A alone (218.00 CZK) is below it, the whole cart (480.00 CZK) is above it — the required asymmetry for an unambiguous test.

facts.answer: NOT APPLIED. The minimum was evaluated against simple-a's own line subtotal (entitled items only), not the whole cart. Even though the whole cart (480 CZK) exceeds the converted minimum (~327 CZK), the discount never fired because simple-a alone (218 CZK) does not.
facts.confidence: high (live, single run; matches the audit's prior static-analysis finding F5 in audit-mvp1-native.md:11)
facts.docsNote: shopify-dev MCP search for 'minimum purchase requirement applies to' / 'minimumRequirement subtotal entitled' returned only schema-reference chunks (DiscountMinimumSubtotal, DiscountPurchaseAmount) with no explicit statement of scope — the live test was the deciding evidence, not a docs quote.

facts.question: Native A (automatic PRODUCT 10% on simple-a) + native B (automatic ORDER 5%, discountClasses=[ORDER] because customerGets.items.all=true) — do they stack when combinesWith disagrees, in both directions?
facts.answer: Do NOT stack in either direction. Both discounts must allow the other's class (mutual agreement) — one side saying no is enough to block combining, regardless of which side it is. When they don't combine, Shopify does not apply both partially: it picked the ORDER discount (B) and dropped the PRODUCT discount (A) entirely in both runs.
facts.docsNote: shopify.dev DiscountCombinesWith reference (admin-graphql/2026-07/objects/DiscountCombinesWith) documents the mutual tag-matching rule for same-class (product-vs-product) combining but does not explicitly spell out the general product-vs-order mutual-agreement rule in the fetched chunks; the live test confirms it end to end.

facts.question: Code discount with 2 redeem codes and usageLimit=1: is the limit per discount (shared across codes) or per code?
facts.answer: Per discount, shared across all its redeem codes. DiscountCodeBasicInput.usageLimit is documented as 'The maximum number of times the discount can be redeemed' (singular 'the discount', not 'the code'). A DiscountRedeemCode is just one of possibly many codes attached to the same DiscountCodeNode; the node carries one usageLimit that all its codes draw down together.
facts.docsQuote: "usage​Limit Int The maximum number of times the discount can be redeemed. For unlimited usage, specify null." — DiscountCodeBasicInput, https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/unstable/input-objects/DiscountCodeBasicInput (same wording on 2026-10 pinned version)
facts.confidence: high (explicit docs wording); live Bogus-checkout order was skipped per the brief's own instruction to skip when docs are explicit

facts.question: Is the 10,000-byte function input limit measured in bytes or characters, and what happens when a metafield exceeds it (with multibyte/Czech text)?
facts.answer: Bytes (UTF-8), not characters. A metafield value over 10,000 bytes is still written and still returned by the GraphQL Admin API, but a Shopify Function's input query receives null for that field instead of erroring. This makes multibyte text (e.g. Czech diacritics, 2 bytes/char in UTF-8) reach the 10,000-byte ceiling at roughly half the character count of ASCII.
facts.docsQuote: "Caution: Shopify Functions input queries don't return metafield values larger than 10,000 bytes. The value is still stored, and the GraphQL Admin API still returns it, but a function receives null for it." — https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/metafields/metafield-limits
facts.liveTestSkippedReason: The brief's own fallback: 'if this is too risky or complex, stop at the docs quote and say so.' A live multibyte-vs-ASCII probe would require writing the shop-level $app:won_discounts/function_config metafield that the REAL 'Won Discounts' automatic node reads in production (confirmed live on 2026-09-29: gid://shopify/Shop/78971076849 already carries a real, non-null function_config — schemaVersion 1, 0 campaigns/rules).
